title: Entropy-Bounded Empiricism: Regime-Dependent Validity in Galaxy Rotation Curves
description: Complete documentation of the Entropy-Bounded Empiricism (EBE) framework applied to the SPARC175 galaxy rotation curves. The paper reports regime-dependent model validity with 100% EFC success in the FLOW regime (62/62) and strong nonparametric evidence (Mann-Whitney p < 0.0001, Cliff's δ = 0.371), while a CMB null test (p = 0.251) shows no regime structure, supporting the framework's specificity to non-equilibrium systems.

key_results.main_finding: EFC achieves 100% success in the FLOW regime (62/62) with strong regime-dependent structure (p < 0.0001, Cliff's δ = 0.371), while the CMB shows no such structure (p = 0.251).
parameters_tested: Kruskal-Wallis H test with Dunn post-hoc

sealed_predictions.statement: Applying the EBE regime-classification pipeline to CMB angular power spectra will show no significant regime structure (p > 0.05, |δ| ≈ 0).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Future high-precision CMB datasets or alternative power spectra analyses yielding significant regime separation under the same pipeline.

kill_criteria: KC1: Pre-registered replication on an independent rotation-curve dataset using fixed thresholds (L1 = 0.337, L2 = 0.427; FLOW: L < 0.337) yields a FLOW EFC success rate ≤ 80% or no significant separation from non-FLOW (Mann–Whitney p ≥ 0.05 and |Cliff's δ| ≤ 0.15).

KC2: After controlling for measurement quality (e.g., N_points stratification or regression adjustment), the regime effect vanishes (p ≥ 0.10 and |δ| ≤ 0.15), indicating the L–quality correlation fully explains the result.

KC3: Robustness failure: Across a pre-specified set of reasonable, model-blind L definitions and small boundary perturbations, ≥ 80% of variants lose significance (p ≥ 0.05) and effect size shrinks to |δ| ≤ 0.15.
KC4: CMB contradiction: Applying the identical regime-classification pipeline to updated CMB angular power spectra finds significant regime structure (p ≤ 0.01 or |δ| ≥ 0.30).

KC5: Information leakage: Demonstration that L (or S) relies on post-fit or model-dependent information; when recomputed with a strictly model-blind definition, the regime effect is not significant (p ≥ 0.05).

KC6: Cross-survey failure: In two or more independent surveys (e.g., THINGS, LITTLE THINGS, SPARC extensions), pre-registered tests with fixed thresholds yield FLOW success rate < 60% (chi-squared < 3) and no significant regime separation (p ≥ 0.05).

KC7: Direct entropy proxy refutation: Independent determinations of low-entropy systems (S < 0.25) identify ≥ 10 galaxies where EFC fits fail strongly (median chi-squared ≥ 5), decoupling FLOW from success.

KC8: Corrected resampling diagnostics: Re-running permutation/bootstrap tests with verified code places the observed effect within the central 90% of the null (p ≥ 0.10), eliminating evidence for non-random regime structure.
KC9: High-quality subsample inconsistency: In the N_points ≥ 50 subsample, FLOW does not outperform other regimes (p ≥ 0.05), contradicting the reported strengthening of the effect with data quality.
abstract_short: EBE framework: 100% EFC success in FLOW regime (62/62 galaxies). Mann-Whitney p<0.0001, Cliff's δ=0.371. CMB null test passes (p=0.251).

ledger_impact.holistic_analysis: This paper establishes the Entropy-Bounded Empiricism (EBE) framework as a rigorous epistemological scaffolding for EFC's domain of validity, demonstrating with nonparametric statistics that EFC achieves 100% success in the FLOW regime (62/62 SPARC galaxies) while the CMB null test confirms no spurious regime structure. It does NOT close any Stage-IV KC or theory gap — it creates a new, self-contained empirical test layer with its own internal kill criteria (EBE-KC1 through EBE-KC5) that are distinct from the five master EFC kill criteria. The paper is a Tier-2 empirical anchor that defines WHERE EFC is expected to work (low-entropy coherent-flow systems) and provides the statistical machinery to test that boundary.
graph_insights: This paper is currently an orphan node in the graph (no 1-2 hop connections found), which means it needs to be explicitly linked to the SPARC rotation-curve validation tests and to the entropy-interpolation formalism in the core EFC theory papers. Without those edges, the EBE results are structurally isolated from the kill-criteria chain.

The concepts 'entropy S' and 'regime classification' should be connected to the EFCLASS Boltzmann solver gap (theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver), since the empirically measured S-boundaries (0.25, 0.65) provide the first data-driven calibration points for the solver's regime-switching logic.
The SPARC node should accumulate this paper alongside any prior SPARC-based EFC tests to build a multi-paper evidence cluster at the galaxy-scale phenomenology layer.

implicit_consequences: The ρ = −0.43 quality-L correlation is an honest vulnerability: EBE-KC2 (quality confound) is the most immediate internal threat and should be prioritized before claiming definitive regime structure.

The 100% FLOW success with zero failures in 62 galaxies is statistically striking but also fragile — a single failure in replication drops the rate and may trigger EBE-KC1. This makes independent replication the single most important next step for this branch.

The CMB null test (p = 0.251) implicitly validates that the regime-classification pipeline is not an overfitting artifact, which strengthens confidence in applying the same pipeline to other non-equilibrium observables (e.g., cluster dynamics, Lyman-α forest).

The EBE framework is explicitly positioned as theory-agnostic ('EFC is used as a concrete test case, not as a prerequisite'), which means any competing model could in principle also be tested within the same regime classification — this is both a strength (scientific credibility) and a strategic exposure (a competitor could claim the FLOW regime).

The L proxy, being model-blind and computed pre-fit, satisfies the information-leakage kill criterion (EBE-KC5) by construction, but this must be independently audited to be credible to external reviewers.

The three-regime structure (FLOW/TRANSITION/LATENT) implicitly maps onto the EFC entropy interpolation S ∈ [0,1], providing the first empirical calibration of which S-ranges correspond to which physical regimes — this constrains the EFCLASS Boltzmann solver (theory-efclass-boltzmann-solver) by fixing the transition boundaries.
